Read back a rating written by export_rating()

Source: R/export_rating.R
import_rating.Rd

Reads a folder made by export_rating() and returns the rating and, if one was exported, its assessment. Before it reads anything, it checks every file against the folder's manifest.csv, so a file that was damaged, truncated or edited afterwards is reported by name and not trusted.

The rating that comes back is the one that went in: the same coefficients, evidence, history, provenance and lifecycle, equal in every value. (It is not identical() in the byte-for-byte sense, which no R object is after being written and read: data.table keeps internal pointers that differ.) A rating saved under an older schema version is migrated if a migration exists, and refused with the reason if not. A rating saved under a newer one is refused: update the package.

Usage

import_rating(path, verify = TRUE)

Arguments

path

Character. A folder made by export_rating().

verify

Logical. If TRUE (default), check every file against the manifest first. Switching it off is for the case where you have already decided the folder is trusted and the manifest is lost.

Value

A list with rating, assessment (NULL if none was exported) and manifest, the checksum table.

See also

export_rating().

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage <- seq(0.3, 3, length.out = 25)
gaugings <- data.frame(stage_m = stage,
                       discharge_cms = 3 * stage^1.6 * exp(rnorm(25, sd = 0.03)))
fit <- fit_rating(gaugings, quiet = TRUE)
folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "example_import")
export_rating(fit, path = folder)

back <- import_rating(folder)
rating_limbs(back$rating)
#>     limb lower_stage_m upper_stage_m       C          a        n
#>    <int>         <num>         <num>   <num>      <num>    <num>
#> 1:     1           0.3             3 3.08768 0.01234489 1.581943
